silhouette.reason: panel-1: From the RTS 3/4 camera the HQ reads well: two conical towers with finials, a steep gable and a pedimented porch with banners make a clear 'faction headquarters'. The tank, crystal ore node and soldiers all read at a glance. In the strict silhouettes the front is a flat box with small bumps, the side is a slab with a detached sliver, and the towers do not stand far enough above the roof ridge to dominate. The plot edge walls are low and add nothing to the outline. | panel-2: From the 3/4 views the base reads at once as an RTS HQ: a gabled hall, two conical-roofed towers, a portico, a tank, a squad and a crystal resource node. In the orthographic silhouettes it falls apart. The front is a flat block with two bumps, and the side is a rectangle with a separate sliver for the plot. Nothing in black says faction, and the hall's roof ridge, portico and towers merge into one mass. The towers are the same height and sit symmetrically, so the outline has no hero accent. | panel-3: The HQ reads clearly as a gabled hall with two conical-roofed towers, a porch and banners, and the tank reads as a tank from the side. But the set is one big box plus low clutter: in silhouette.png the side view is a plain rectangle with a stub, the infantry and crystal node vanish into the base slab, and the two towers are identical so nothing marks this as one specific faction. Tower finials and the flag are the only fine accents.
fixes: Raise the towers about 1.5-2 m above the ridge and add a corbelled parapet or machicolation ring under the cones so they break the outline
Add a ridge feature (chimney, signal mast or a central belfry) so the front and side silhouettes are not one flat box
Give the perimeter wall a gate or corner posts so the plot edge has a readable profile
Make one tower clearly taller (about 1.4x) with a spire or a faction finial so the outline has a dominant vertical
Push the portico forward and raise its gable above the eave line so it breaks the front silhouette
Add tall faction elements on the plot (a flag mast taller than the ridge, or a radar or antenna on the HQ) so the side view is more than a slab
Break the hall's box: add a chimney or command mast with antenna/dish on the ridge, dormers on the roof slope and a taller, differently capped second tower so the two towers are not mirror copies
Give the roof a visible overhang and ridge cresting so the SIDE outline is not a rectangle
Raise the crystal node (taller central shard, 2.5-3 m) and add a harvester rig or derrick beside it so the resource reads in black
Give infantry a readable outline: helmet brim, rifle held clear of the torso, backpack and antenna on the squad leader

proportions.reason: panel-1: Overall 30x25x11.2 m with a roughly 18 m hall and a tank of about 6-7 m is plausible next to 1.8 m soldiers. Problems: the side view shows the roof slab running out past the porch with a thin awning hanging off it, so the porch roof looks stuck on rather than framed into the gable. The window streaks hang below the sills like icicles and visually stretch the wall. The tank turret is very large and set far back for its hull, and the soldiers read as stiff mannequins with oversized heads and backpacks. | panel-2: The overall 30x25x11.2 m footprint is plausible for an RTS HQ plot, and soldiers at about 1.8 m sit right against the doors. Several things are off by eye. The tower doors are squat and narrow next to the tall hall windows. The portico columns are spindly for the gable they carry. The tank looks undersized next to the soldiers: the hull is barely three figures long, and the turret is oversized and domed like a toy. The perimeter wall is only waist-high and stops short, so the yard reads as an open slab rather than an enclosure. | panel-3: Scale between building, tank and soldiers is plausible on the 5 m grid (door height against figures, tank about 6-7 m long). Weaknesses: the infantry are mannequins with oversized spherical heads, cylinder limbs, no neck and no hands or feet shaping; the towers are fat and short for their caps; the hall's storey height is tall relative to the single row of small windows, leaving a large blank wall band under the eave; the porch posts are thin for the pediment they carry; the perimeter wall is knee-to-waist height and thick, reading as a kerb rather than a defensive wall.
fixes: Frame the porch roof into the main gable with matching pitch and posts that carry it, instead of an awning protruding past the side wall
Shrink the tank turret about 15% and move it forward to sit over the hull middle
Reduce soldier head size to about 1/7.5 of body height and add bent knees/arms variation so they do not read as identical mannequins
Scale the tank hull to about 6.5-7 m long and reduce the turret to about 45% of the hull length
Raise the tower doors to 2.1-2.4 m and thicken the portico columns to about 1/8 of their height
Run the perimeter wall around the whole plot, or end it at gate piers, so the enclosure reads as intended
Rebuild the infantry at 7.5 heads tall: head about 0.23 m, real neck, tapered limbs, boots and hands, shoulders wider than hips
Slim the towers (diameter about 0.8x) and raise them one course above the hall eave before the cone starts
Add a second window row or a string course and cornice to fill the blank wall band under the eave
Thicken porch posts to about 0.35 m with bases and capitals; raise the perimeter wall to 1.2-1.5 m or turn it into proper jersey barriers with gaps

materials.reason: panel-1: Stone, red roof shingles, dark timber posts, sandbags and crates separate by hue. The tank hull and the rock show no metal or wet sheen; everything has the same mid roughness under raking light. Windows are flat saturated yellow emissive with no glazing or interior. The crystals are flat orange with no translucency or glow, and the red roof is a uniform hue across every shingle. | panel-2: Stone, red roof tile, timber, wall caps and tank paint separate by hue, but nearly everything shares the same matte roughness. The tank shows no metal response, the crystals look like flat orange plastic with no translucency or rim glow, and the windows are flat unlit yellow with no frame depth or interior. The grey squares on the roof read as pasted decals, not missing or replaced tiles. The grey translucent spikes under the windows read as icicles, not stains. | panel-3: Stone block, timber posts, clay tile and painted tank armour separate by hue and value, and the tile roof has a believable sheen. But the windows are flat emissive yellow cards with no glass, reveal depth or reflection; the crystals are opaque orange plastic with no translucency or glow; the ground slab is one uniform grey concrete with only a dark gravel strip; banner cloth is a flat dark red plane with no weave or fold; infantry are a single glossy putty material so cloth, skin and metal do not separate; the tank tracks and wheels are barely darker than the hull.
fixes: Give the tank exposed steel (track links, barrel muzzle, hatch edges) a metallic, lower-roughness slot so it catches light
Replace flat emissive windows with a glass slot plus a dimmer warm interior and a frame reflection
Vary roof shingle albedo per tile by plus or minus 8% value and add a translucent/emissive core to the crystals
Give the tank hull and tracks a metal finish with edge highlights, and give the tracks a dark rubber or steel roughness
Give the crystals an emissive core plus a translucent or rim finish so they read as an energy resource
Recess the windows with frame depth and use a warm emissive gradient instead of a flat fill
Replace the opaque grey roof squares with darker gaps or slightly offset tiles, and turn the under-window spikes into soft albedo streaks
Model window reveals 0.15 m deep with a glass pane (low roughness, slight reflection) in front of a dimmer warm interior, plus frames in timber
Give crystals an emissive core, lower roughness and a transmission/optics preset so they read as mineral, not plastic
Split infantry paint slots: matte cloth uniform, skin, dark metal weapon, leather webbing
Break the ground into packed dirt, paved apron and worn concrete with different roughness; darken tracks to rubber/steel with bright worn metal on the running faces
Add fold geometry and a cloth strip with sheen to the banners

detail.reason: panel-1: LOD0 has real shingles, coursed stone blocks, window muntins, timber framing, track wheels and rivets on the tank, crates and sandbags. It holds up at RTS zoom but not in a close-up: soldiers are lumpy primitives, the plinth and walls are plain boxes with panel lines only, the porch interior is a dark void, and the tower door and arrow slits are flat insets. The detail heatmap shows triangle density spread evenly over flat walls instead of concentrated on the hero features. | panel-2: Up close the stone coursing, half-timber posts, shingle rows, tank road wheels and sandbags hold up reasonably at third-person distance. The soldiers are crude peg figures with ball heads and no readable faces, hands or kit. The tank has almost no hatches, tools, bolts or vision blocks. Doors, sills, gutters and downpipes are missing on the hall, and the crystal node has no base debris or extraction hardware. | panel-3: The detail heat map shows density concentrated on the hall walls and roof, while the ground, which is most of the frame, is nearly empty. Stone coursing, tile rows, window mullions, tank bolts, sandbags and crates are present and at a sane scale. In close-up (raking_detail.png) it does not hold: the grey roof patches are arbitrary flat rectangles, the streaks under the sills are crude vertical wedges, the door is a plain plank panel, there are no gutters, downpipes, hinges, lamps, cables or signage, the infantry have no faces, gear straps or hands, and 148k triangles buy surprisingly little visible detail.
fixes: Model the porch interior: double door, steps with nosings and lanterns on the columns
Add window sills, lintels and quoins at the building corners and tower base
Give soldiers helmets, rifles with slings and boots as separate forms instead of capsule stacks
Sculpt the soldiers with helmets, faces, gloves and webbing pouches
Add commander and driver hatches, tow hooks, a tool rack and track guards to the tank
Add gutters, downpipes, door hardware and window sills to the hall
Add a harvester pad or scattered shards at the base of the crystal node
Replace the random grey roof rectangles with slipped/missing tiles showing battens, plus ridge tiles, gutters and downpipes at the eaves
Add door ironwork (strap hinges, handle, studs), lintels and sills in relief, wall lamps by the entrance and a faction crest in relief rather than a flat yellow disc
Dress the yard: tyre ruts, oil stains, cable runs, fuel drums with bands, ammo boxes with stencils, a radio mast, floodlights
Give infantry helmets, webbing, pouches, boots and a modelled rifle with stock and magazine
Add tank tools, tow cable, hatches with hinges, exhausts and track links that read individually at LOD0

wear.reason: panel-1: There is an attempt: grey missing-shingle squares on the roof, dark streaks under windows, some tank dirt. But the roof patches are evenly scattered identical grey squares that read as a pattern, not damage, and the window streaks are sharp-edged pointed shapes that read as icicles. No moss at the wall base, no chipped stone edges, no track ruts in the gravel, no dust on the tank lower hull. The perimeter walls and ground slab are perfectly clean. | panel-2: There is some attempt at wear: streaks below the windows, camo weathering on the tank and scattered roof tile breakup. It reads as procedural noise rather than history. The roof squares sit on a regular grid, the streaks look like icicles, and there are no tyre or track marks on the yard even though a tank is parked there. The walls have no chips, and grime does not collect at the wall base or tower plinths. | panel-3: There is some story: replaced grey roof tiles, drip streaks below the sills, darker stone at the tower base, chipped red paint on the tank and worn track ruts in the gravel. It is thin and mechanical: the streaks are identical wedges repeated under every window, the roof patches are uniformly scattered, the ground and perimeter walls are clean and uniform, the banners are pristine, and there is no dirt build-up where walls meet ground, no moss, soot, tyre marks or damage from use.
fixes: Cluster missing shingles near the eaves and ridge with exposed battens, and drop the even grey-square scatter
Replace the pointed streak meshes with soft vertex-colour rain streaks that fade downward
Add mud and dust on the tank lower hull and tracks, track ruts on the gravel path, and grime/moss along the wall bases
Add track ruts and oil stains on the gravel and paving leading to the tank bay
Darken the AO and grime at wall bases, tower plinths and under eaves, and chip the edges of the wall caps
Randomise where the replaced roof tiles fall (clustered near the ridge and eaves) and vary their tone
Vary drip streaks per window by seed (length, width, opacity) and soften them into the stone instead of hard wedges
Add ground-contact grime: a dark splash band along the wall base, mud near the gravel road, oil under the tank parking spot
Chip and stain the perimeter wall tops and corners; crack one or two blocks
Fray and fade the banner hems, add soot above the chimney/vents and moss or lichen on the north roof slope
Cluster roof repairs in one or two areas rather than even scatter, and sag the ridge slightly

fixes: Keep the gold gable emblem as a low-poly disc at LOD2; it is a faction marker
Bake the stone coursing and roof patches into vertex colour at LOD2 so the value pattern does not pop
Keep the half-timber posts as cheap boxes at LOD1 and LOD2; they cost a few triangles and carry the facade rhythm
Bake the stone coursing into the LOD2 vertex colour or trim UVs so the walls do not go flat beige
Keep the gable emblem as a single flat disc at LOD2 since it is a large high-contrast colour block
Bake the roof patch value into LOD2 vertex colour so the roof does not turn cleaner and redder
Keep tower finials and the flag as 2-4 triangle slivers, and keep the timber posts as vertex-colour bands on the wall
Match LOD2 window size to the LOD0 opening and keep the curved apron outline with a few segments

technical.reason: panel-1: QA is clean. But 148k triangles at LOD0 for an RTS base, which will be seen from high above, is heavy, and the density heatmap shows triangles spread over flat stone walls and ground rather than on the silhouette features. LOD1 at 35k is still large for RTS use. LOD2 at 3.9k is sensible. | panel-2: QA is clean and the LOD ratios (148k to 35k to 3.9k) are sensible. But 148k triangles at LOD0 is very heavy for an RTS base seen mostly from a high camera. Much of it is probably spent on shingles and stone blocks, while the tank, soldiers and crystals stay crude. | panel-3: QA is clean and the LOD ladder (148k / 35k / 3.9k) has sensible ratios. But 148k triangles at LOD0 for an RTS diorama of this visual fidelity is poorly spent: the heat map shows density packed into wall coursing and tiles that read as texture from any gameplay distance, while the infantry, ground and props that need form are starved. LOD2 at 3.9k is reasonable for the whole set, though a single hall plus units would normally ship as separate assets with their own pivots.
fixes: Cut LOD0 toward 60-80k by moving stone-block and shingle relief to the normal map, keeping geometry for the silhouette, the porch and the tank
Bring LOD1 to about 12-15k by dropping individual shingles and soldier detail
Cut the roof shingles to trim-sheet strips at LOD0 and move that triangle budget into the soldiers, the tank and the crystal node
Aim for about 60-80k triangles at LOD0 for a diorama this size
Move stone coursing and tile rows from geometry to the trim sheet normal/height and cut LOD0 to roughly 60-80k, spending the savings on infantry, tank and yard props
Split the faction into separately pivoted parts (hall, tank, squad, resource node) so engines can instance and animate them
Lower LOD1 toward 20k by dropping per-tile and per-block geometry first
